definition: A frontier model appearing across 3 sources as an agent backbone and an evaluation subject. Its most consequential archived result is as the backbone for a diagnosis-guided recovery harness, where the same model goes from 40.13 to 91.94 percent on an embodied benchmark and from 18.32 to 74.90 on a multi-application one -- and where the matched-information rerun shows the gain belongs to the recovery interface rather than to privileged information. It also appears in contamination-mitigation evaluation and in a financial benchmark where unit and scale perturbations collapse the strongest models.

evidence.note: Shows that the standard metric for judging contamination-mitigation strategies can be scored by cancellation rather than by restoration, replaces it with a per-question stratified metric under which the published ranking reverses, and proposes a mitigation that decides its intervention during decoding instead of from a prior estimate.
evidence.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Probability Evaluation and Step-wise Mitigation of Benchmark Contamination

evidence.note: Generates financial reasoning benchmarks from executable computation trees over real tables so that answers are correct by construction with no model in the labelling loop, exposes four independently controllable difficulty axes, and finds that unit and scale perturbations collapse the strongest model from 98.4 percent to 3.0.
evidence.title: V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark

evidence.note: Profiles the dominant failure mode of an agent task family on development data, then freezes a policy that permits only the recovery interventions matched to that failure -- so a failure decides which repair is admissible and how much evidence to spend, rather than triggering more context indiscriminately.
evidence.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
